title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: The tape tells you what institutions are actually doing with their money, even when the valuation makes value investors uncomfortable.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Adaptation

Shares sit +11.92% above the rising 30-week SMA (₹2,848.03) with daily RSI at 55.31 [22].

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Our stop ratchet and supply audit work together. As the 30-week SMA climbed to ₹2,848.03, our hard stop moved up from ₹2,696.82 to ₹2,789.41 (+₹92.59). Meanwhile, 8 distribution days, -16.6% 28-day relative strength, and expiring PE lock-ins equal to ~42–46 days of volume explain why trimming half our stake (50 shares) at ₹3,187.50 is prudent gap-risk management.

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 was the cold shower of 109x P/E valuation math and our reconciled ₹2,200.00 Base fair value, Chapter 8 is where we read the actual footprints of institutional capital on the NSE tape. And here, we must stay completely objective: SEDEMAC is not yet breaking down. On pure price-volatility compression, the stock has tightened into a 7.0% Bollinger-bandwidth Stage 2 coil—yet underneath the surface, distribution days, lagging relative strength, and an expiring PE block-deal lock-in flash unmistakable caution.

Let us keep our two session cutoffs crystal clear so no indicator is ever misread. On the verified 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close, SEDEMAC ended at ₹3,118.40 (+1.42% on the day) on 92,543 shares—0.89x its 20-day average volume—with a rising 50-day SMA at ₹3,160.53 (putting the Nov 23 close -1.33% below the 50-day SMA and -0.16% below the 10-week EMA) and a daily RSI of 50.39. Because the stock listed on March 11, 2026, it has only 173 daily trading bars, so the mechanical daily ledger still prints 'N/A (insufficient history)' for the 200-day moving average. Two sessions later, on the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot close, SEDEMAC gained +2.22% to ₹3,187.50, reclaiming its 50-day SMA (₹3,171.07, +0.52% extension), lifting daily RSI to 55.31, and moving +2.06% above its 10-week EMA (₹3,123.31).

Look at the weekly structural floor beneath the stock: the rising 30-week SMA has climbed ₹90.12 over the past two weeks, moving from ₹2,757.91 on November 13 to ₹2,848.03 on November 25. Price now sits +11.92% above that rising 30-week anchor. Simultaneously, daily Bollinger bandwidth has compressed from 7.2% down to 7.0%, while the 63-day volume dry-up ratio sits at 0.20 and 2026-11-25 volume came in at 85,112 shares (0.80x the 30-day average of 105,887). On the intraday chart, 4-hour momentum turned cleanly upward (4H RSI 60.45 above 4H EMA20 ₹3,109.23 and 4H SMA50 ₹3,104.63).

Yet a veteran tape reader never looks at price compression without asking who owns the overhead supply. Between March and September 2026, foreign institutional investors quadrupled their stake from 2.52% to 10.30%, absorbing early domestic fund selling (DIIs dipped from 43.93% to 38.34%) while promoters held rock-steady at 26.23% with zero pledged shares. Even as retail shareholder count climbed 75% from 18,127 to 31,794, total public float actually tightened from 27.31% to 25.12%.

What changed in our November 25 refresh is a material institutional supply overhang that directly threatens a closing stop on an illiquid stock. Following the September 10, 2026 six-month IPO lock-in expiry, pre-IPO institutional backers—A91 Emerging Fund, Xponentia Opportunities Fund, and HDFC Life—sold roughly 10% of the company (~44.3 to 48.79 lakh shares, equal to ~42–46 days of 30-day average daily volume) in September 24 block deals, agreeing to a 60-day lock-in on further sales. On November 18, 2026, financial press reports flagged renewed block-deal supply risk as that 60-day lock-in expires. Add in NSE Circular CML77614 on November 20, 2026 listing fresh ESOP shares (following the November 13 in-principle approval for 1.215 lakh shares within the ~9.75 lakh ESOP 2025 pool), and you see why the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger counts 8 distribution days in 25 sessions and why 28-day relative strength against the Nifty 50 lags at -16.6% (-9.0% over 63 days).

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A tight 7.0% Bollinger squeeze above a rising 30-week SMA (₹2,848.03) justifies keeping a right-sized 50-share core stake working for you—never panic-sell an intact Stage 2 trend wholesale. Yet an expiring PE block-deal lock-in equal to 42–46 days of volume, 8 distribution days, -16.6% 28-day relative strength, and a 109x P/E demand cutting exposure in half before a discounted block gaps through your closing stop.

book_subsections.title: The Upward-Only Stop-Loss Ratchet: Lifting Our Hard Floor from ₹2,696.82 to ₹2,789.41
paragraphs: One of our most binding risk rules for held Stage 2 positions is the upward-only stop-loss ratchet: as a winner's weekly moving averages climb beneath price, we trail our structural exit higher to lock in gains and never widen a stop downward. On November 13, 2026, when SEDEMAC's 30-week SMA stood at ₹2,757.91, our hard invalidation stop was anchored at ₹2,696.82.

By November 25, 2026, the rising 30-week SMA has advanced to ₹2,848.03, Pivot S1 sits at ₹2,869.40, and the 63-day base low sits at ₹2,794.80. Accordingly, our live TradingView invalidation stop ratchets cleanly upward by +₹92.59 (+3.43%) to ₹2,789.41. Notice the geometry of ₹2,789.41: with 14-day ATR at ₹117.25 (3.68% of the live ₹3,187.50 close), ₹2,789.41 sits roughly 3.4 ATRs below current price and cleanly beneath both the 30-week SMA (₹2,848.03) and the 63-day base low (₹2,794.80). That gives our right-sized 50-share core position room to absorb routine ₹100–₹150 daily swings without getting shaken out prematurely, while guaranteeing an exit if a PE block deal or earnings disappointment breaks the primary weekly uptrend.

On the upside, immediate resistance sits at Pivot Middle (₹3,259.70), followed by Pivot R1 at ₹3,509.40 and the 52-week peak at ₹3,650.00. A decisive breakout above ₹3,509.40 would require daily volume expanding cleanly above 140,000–160,000 shares (roughly 1.5x the 30-day average of 105,887) to prove institutions are absorbing A91, Xponentia, or HDFC Life block supply. Even if that breakout occurs, however, our timing posture stays capped at wait-for-support and our 109x P/E valuation gate blocks fresh capital completely.

book_subsections.title: Cash-Equity Risk Discipline in a Narrow-Breadth Nifty Regime Without NSE F&O
paragraphs: Our November 25 options-eligibility audit reconfirms that SEDEMAC is not part of the NSE F&O segment and offers zero listed derivatives liquidity. Unlike large-cap Indian stocks or liquid US equities where a portfolio manager can buy protective puts ahead of a PE block-deal expiry or express upside via defined-risk call spreads, SEDEMAC's risk must be managed strictly through cash-equity position sizing and hard closing stop-loss discipline.

That cash-equity constraint matters even more given the broader Indian market regime on the verified 2026-11-23 NSE ledger. Nifty 50 sits in a narrow-breadth uptrend with 55.2% of the 500-stock universe above its 50-day SMA, 48.2% above its 200-day SMA, 7 of 11 sectors above their 50-day SMA, and 3 distribution days. In a narrow-breadth tape where barely half of mid-caps are holding their 200-day moving averages, a 109x P/E stock trading 65,000–106,000 shares a day can experience sharp air pockets if an institutional block prints at a 5%–8% discount to market.

Let us walk through the exact multi-timeframe dashboard you should monitor on TradingView over the coming weeks. On the 4-hour chart, watch whether price holds above 4H EMA20 (₹3,109.23) and 4H SMA50 (₹3,104.63) with 4H RSI staying above 50. On the daily chart, watch the 20-day SMA (₹3,104.92) and 50-day SMA (₹3,171.07) support band (₹3,076.46–₹3,218.64) and monitor whether distribution days cool below 6 in a 25-session window. On the weekly chart, the 10-week EMA (₹3,123.31) and rising 30-week SMA (₹2,848.03) define the primary trend; as long as SEDEMAC closes above ₹2,789.41, our right-sized 50-share house-money stake (~3.66% weight) stays invested. A daily close below ₹2,789.41 ends the benefit of the doubt immediately.

Put together, Chapter 8 hands us a crisp operational rulebook: trim 50 shares immediately ahead of the expiring PE lock-in, keep 50 core shares riding above the rising 30-week SMA with a secondary 25-share trim at ₹3,450.00, ratchet the hard stop upward from ₹2,696.82 to ₹2,789.41, and never let a tight chart coil—especially alongside 8 distribution days and -16.6% 28-day relative strength—tempt you into deploying fresh capital at 109x trailing earnings.

One final institutional nuance worth tracking on the tape is how SEDEMAC behaves relative to its own Auto Parts: OEM peer group. On our November 25 TheWrap Stage 2 scan, Auto Parts: OEM carries a sub-50% sector Stage 2 density of 43.4% (ranked 24th across Indian industry groups), with SEDEMAC posting a 91.1 relative-strength percentile and ₹171.22 Cr in average weekly turnover. That liquidity profile—roughly ₹27 Cr to ₹35 Cr of daily cash turnover—is ample for retail exits, yet thin enough that a single ₹300 Cr to ₹500 Cr secondary block from A91 Emerging Fund, Xponentia, or HDFC Life represents two full weeks of normal market volume. Watching whether institutional buyers absorb that secondary supply cleanly above ₹3,076–₹3,123 without breaking the 10-week EMA will tell us immediately whether foreign funds still have appetite to defend a triple-digit multiple.
